gotchas.procedure_section: Review - Kid Taxes and Filings (separate client ID / project code)
gotchas.title: Ethan cannot go on Form 8814
gotchas.trap: Follow the client's request / PY return and report Ethan's $6,400 UTMA income on the parents' return via Form 8814.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Form 8814 is available only if the child's income is solely interest and dividends (incl. capital gain distributions) and < $13,500. Ethan has a $3,100 capital gain from a fund SALE and $3,200 of wages -> not eligible. Unearned income $6,400 > $2,700 -> Form 8615 on Ethan's own return. Separate client ID EVG1021 and 1040 project code opened.
gotchas.impact: Parents' return must show nothing for Ethan; Ethan's return EVG1021 carries the kiddie tax

gotchas.title: Chloe's $1,900 interest - Form 8814 election
gotchas.trap: Either ignore Chloe's 1099-INT (below $2,700 so 'nothing to report') or add $1,900 to the parents' interest income.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Chloe must file (unearned > $1,350) unless parents elect Form 8814. Elected: line 4 $1,900 < $2,700 base -> $0 added to parents' income; tax 10% x ($1,900 - $1,350) = $55 added to Form 1040 line 16. Trade-off: identical tax to a separate return for Chloe, one fewer return and fee; no AGI-based items of the parents are affected because $0 is included.

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule D - missing cost basis on Consolidated 1099 (equity comp)
gotchas.title: RSU shares reported with $0 basis
gotchas.trap: Autoflow takes the 1099-B basis of $0 -> $69,338 of proceeds taxed as gain (the $86,400 of 2025 vest income and the 2023 lot income were already taxed as W-2 wages).
gotchas.correct_treatment: Form 8949 box B (short-term) / box E (long-term) - basis not reported to IRS; enter 1099-B basis $0, code B, and a negative column (g) adjustment equal to FMV at vest from the supplemental statement. Net RSU gain $9,458 (ST $788, LT $8,670).

gotchas.procedure_section: Scan - unstructured documents / Payment-app export (household employee)
gotchas.title: Nanny treated as a 1099 contractor
gotchas.trap: Accept the client's 1099-NEC treatment (or ignore it - 'not our client's income') and file with no Schedule H.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Maria is a household employee (family controls when/how the work is done, in their home, their car, weekly pay, no other clients). Cash wages $28,000 >= $2,800 (2025) -> Schedule H: SS/Medicare 15.3% = $4,284; FUTA 0.6% x $7,000 = $42 (WA ESD contributions paid by 04/15/2026) -> $4,326 on Schedule 2 line 9. Obtain EIN, file W-2/W-3 (box 1 includes the $2,142 employee share paid by the employer), file corrected $0 1099-NEC, register with WA ESD; 2024 wages $6,240 also exceeded the 2024 $2,700 threshold -> amend 2024 (separate project).

gotchas.title: Dependent-care FSA displaces the credit
gotchas.trap: Claim a $600 credit (20% x $3,000) for Chloe's nanny costs in addition to the $5,000 FSA exclusion.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Only Chloe (under 13) is a qualifying person (Ethan is 16). With one qualifying person the credit base is $3,000 - $5,000 excluded FSA benefits = $0. Form 2441 is still required (Part III) to support the $5,000 exclusion and list the provider (Maria, SSN).

gotchas.title: 529 distribution for private K-12 tuition
gotchas.trap: Treat the $3,123 earnings in box 2 as taxable (no 1098-T), or claim an education credit for the tuition.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Up to $10,000 per year per beneficiary of K-12 tuition is a qualified expense for 2025 (the $20,000 limit starts 2026). Distribution $10,000 = qualified tuition -> $0 taxable; nothing on the 1040. K-12 tuition is not eligible for AOTC/LLC.

gotchas.title: High-income phase-outs and surtaxes
gotchas.trap: Full $4,400 CTC; skip Form 8959 because the employer 'already withheld Additional Medicare'; skip NIIT.
gotchas.correct_treatment: CTC reduced $50 per $1,000 of MAGI over $400,000 -> $1,950. Form 8959: combined Medicare wages $463,350 - $250,000 MFJ threshold x 0.9% = $1,920; employer withheld only $1,200 (on Daniel's wages over $200,000) - credited on line 25c. NIIT 3.8% x NII $18,928 = $719.

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule A - sales tax vs income tax (no-income-tax state)
gotchas.title: WA residents: general sales tax election
gotchas.trap: Enter $0 on line 5a (no state income tax), or add both PFML premiums and sales tax.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Elect general sales taxes (IRS calculator / Axcess blended-rate option): $3,912 > PFML premiums treated as income tax. Only one of income or sales tax may be itemized. Itemized total exceeds the $31,500 standard deduction.

software_exceptions.title: RSU sales reported with $0 basis (basis not reported to IRS)
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: AutoFlow imported the Summit Shareworks 1099-B as reported - six sales, proceeds $69,338, basis $0 - and Schedule D showed ~$70,545 of gain (with the CG distributions). The FMV at vest ($59,880 for the lots sold) was already taxed as W-2 wages; Axcess cannot see the employer's supplemental statement.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Gains and Losses > Form 8949: box B (short-term: four sell-to-cover sales + 12/05 sale) / box E (150 sh from the 03/15/2023 release); keep 1099-B basis $0, adjustment code B, column (g) = -FMV at vest per lot (total $59,880). Net RSU gain $9,458 (ST $788, LT $8,670). Tie W-2 box 14 RSU $86,400 to the release schedule.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - ProConnect computes gain from the basis entered; $0 from the 1099-B means the full proceeds are taxed.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Dispositions screen: per lot, cost basis $0 as reported plus adjustment code B and the FMV-at-vest adjustment (or enter the corrected basis with code B) - field per current release - verify.
software_exceptions.procedure_section: Schedule D - missing cost basis on Consolidated 1099 (equity comp)
software_exceptions.notes: Sell-to-cover lots STC1/STC2/STC4 show small losses ($22.80/$5.70/$22.80): the retained shares come from the same release, no other NSCS purchases in any account - no wash-sale adjustment taken (de minimis $51; firm position).

software_exceptions.title: Kid taxes: Ethan not eligible for Form 8814 (fund sale + wages); Chloe 8814 elected
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Following the client's request and the 2024 return, Form 8814 was set up for both children. Form 8814 has lines only for interest, ordinary dividends and capital gain distributions, so Ethan's $3,100 gain from a fund SALE (and his W-2) simply never enters the calculation - Axcess produces a tidy but invalid 8814 with no diagnostic.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Delete Ethan's Form 8814 from the parents' return. Ethan files his own 1040 with Form 8615 (separate client ID EVG1021, own project code); parents' information for his 8615: taxable income $402,319, tax, qualified dividends $5,904, net capital gain $9,877 (Axcess parent-information input on the child's return - verify field path). Chloe's 8814 stays: $1,900 interest < $2,700 -> $0 added to income; tax $55 on line 16.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same Form 8814 limitation. Ethan's return needs Form 8615 and ProConnect has no Family Link (a Lacerte feature): the parents' figures must be keyed manually; until they are, diagnostic ref 826 ('Form 8615 must be filed').
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Parents' return: Children's Interest and Dividends (8814) for Chloe only. Ethan's return: Taxes > Children Under 18 (8615) > Parent's Information - parents' TI $402,319, tax, filing status MFJ; re-check if the parents' return changes.
software_exceptions.proconnect_reference: Intuit help: 'How do you generate Form 8615 in ProConnect Tax'; 'resolve diagnostic Ref 826'
software_exceptions.procedure_section: Review - Kid Taxes and Filings (separate client ID / project code)
software_exceptions.notes: Ethan's return must be finalized after the parents' (export of final TI).

software_exceptions.title: Nanny paid on a 1099-NEC is a household employee - Schedule H
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: The organizer answered 'no household employees' and the clients issued Maria a 1099-NEC (not the taxpayers' income, so nothing AutoFlows). No Schedule H exists unless the preparer creates it; total tax is understated $4,326 with no diagnostic.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Other Taxes > Household employment taxes (Schedule H): cash wages $28,000; SS/Medicare 15.3% = $4,284 (employee share paid by employer - not withheld); FUTA wages $7,000 x 0.6% = $42 with state contributions paid 04/06/2026 (line 14 'Yes'); total $4,326 to Schedule 2 line 9. W-2 box 1 for Maria $30,142 (employee FICA paid by employer is income-tax wages only) - prepared outside the 1040.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - Schedule H is generated only from household employment inputs.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Household Employment Taxes (Schedule H) screen: cash wages $28,000, FUTA wages $7,000, state contributions paid timely (screen/field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.efile_impact: None (Schedule H e-filed with the 1040; W-2/W-3 filed with SSA separately)

software_exceptions.title: 1099-Q for private K-12 tuition - earnings not taxable
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: The 1099-Q AutoFlowed and the draft showed box 2 earnings $3,123 as other income. The education worksheet treats a 529 distribution as taxable unless qualified expenses are entered; there is no 1098-T for K-12 tuition, so nothing is matched automatically.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Education > 1099-Q / qualified expenses input: enter K-12 tuition $10,000 (Lakeside Hills Academy, grade 7) as a qualified 529 expense (verify field path in current release) -> taxable earnings $0. No education credit (K-12 tuition is not a credit expense).
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - 1099-Q earnings are taxable unless qualified expenses are entered.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Education > 1099-Q: enter qualified K-12 tuition expenses $10,000 for Chloe (field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.notes: 2025 limit $10,000 per beneficiary for K-12 tuition (rises to $20,000 from 2026 under OBBBA).
